evals.prompt: Add `src/skills/case-triage.skill.ts` for our support app: the assistant should be able to query and read support cases and run our existing `crm_escalate_case` Action on a case. Only activate it when the user is working on the `support_case` object. None of the project's files are in this directory: write the file in your answer.
evals.expected_output: Emits a `defineSkill` with a snake_case `name`, `label`, `instructions`, and a `tools` list where every name resolves: platform tools `query_records` / `get_record` plus the action tool `action_crm_escalate_case` materialised from the stack's own Action. Routing is a `triggerConditions` entry `{ field: 'objectName', operator: 'eq', value: 'support_case' }` (a string value for `eq`). No `permissions` key on the skill (removed in 17) and no `*.agent.ts` file.

evals.prompt: Our copilot should use Anthropic with a low temperature (0.3) and cap responses at 2000 tokens. Where do these settings go in the metadata?
evals.expected_output: Places sampling under the agent's `model` block (`AIModelConfigSchema`): `provider: 'anthropic'`, a free-string `model`, `temperature: 0.3` (0–2, outside is a parse error) and `maxTokens: 2000`. States that there is no top-level `temperature` / `maxTokens` on an agent and that the inline `provider` enum is `openai | azure_openai | anthropic | local`.

evals.prompt: Index our `kb_article` records (title and body) so the assistant can answer from them with RAG. Only published articles, and we want to filter by `category` at search time. We run RAGFlow.
evals.expected_output: Emits a `KnowledgeSourceSchema.parse({...})` record with `adapter: 'ragflow'` and `source: { kind: 'object', object: 'kb_article', contentFields: ['title', 'body'], metadataFields: ['category'], where: { published: true } }`, `refresh: { onRecordChange: true }`, registered at boot through `KnowledgeServicePlugin({ sources })`. Chunking / top-K / rerankers are adapter config, not platform metadata.

evals.prompt: Write a `*.tool.ts` so the assistant can call our `crm_close_case` action on a support case. None of the project's files are in this directory: write the file in your answer.
evals.expected_output: Does not author a tool record: the default path is to opt the Action in with `ai: { exposed: true, description: '<40+ chars>' }` on the object's action, which materialises `action_crm_close_case`, and to name that tool in a skill's `tools`. `defineTool` is only for presentation refinement and cannot make anything executable (no `handler` / `implementation`; `ToolSchema` is strict).

evals.prompt: Create `src/ai/support-bot.agent.ts` with defineAgent({ name: 'crm_support_bot', tools: ['query_records', 'action_crm_close_case'], knowledge: ['support_kb'] }) and register it under agents. None of the project's files are in this directory: answer from what is stated here.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the agent: the `agent` type is closed to third parties (a stack-authored agent is filtered out, refused by `loadAgent()` and 404s on chat), and `agent.tools` / `agent.knowledge` are protocol-17 tombstones. Re-declares the two tools in a `defineSkill` (registered under `skills`) with a `surface`, and restricts retrieval at the knowledge-source level (`aiExposed`, `where`) rather than on an agent. The runtime's `ask` / `build` agents pick the skill up by surface.

evals.prompt: Write a nightly operator script that uses `@objectstack/client` with our API token to go through the AI pending-actions queue and approve every pending item older than a day.
evals.expected_output: Does not decide on the token: the script may list the queue (`client.ai.pendingActions.list({ status: 'pending' })`), but approving or rejecting an item is the person's own act, done in the app on their signed-in session by the person the assistant call ran as. An API key or token is refused on the decide door, even the person's own, and so is an AI identity; another user's `ai:approve` does not decide the item, and the model's own confirmation does not count. The script reports or notifies the stale items instead; where a second person must approve the write, that is the approvals engine's `held` outcome.

evals.prompt: Our MCP agent runs the `crm_close_deal` action, which declares `ai.requiresConfirmation: true`. It asks the user in chat, then calls `run_action` again with `confirm: true`, and that call is now refused. Fix how the agent handles this action.
evals.expected_output: Stop sending `confirm`: `run_action` and `resume_run` refuse any call that carries the member, on every action, because the agent cannot confirm for the person. Call `run_action({ actionName: 'crm_close_deal', recordId })` without it. Where the host registers a pending-confirmation service, the answer is `status: 'pending_confirmation'` with a `pendingId` and a message: that is a success, not an error, and nothing has run. Relay the message, tell the user to approve it in the app, and do not retry. On a host with no such service (the open-source build ships none) the call is refused 428 `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with `details.reason: 'no_confirmation_service'`, and the person performs the action in the app. The two delete tools still take the member.

evals.prompt: Our host bridges its action tools onto the stdio MCP server. A desktop client calls `run_action` on an action declaring `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` and the user sees a question in the client. What does each answer do? And what happens when our unattended agent calls the same action under its own AI service account key?
evals.expected_output: The client advertised form-mode `elicitation`, so the person is asked once in the client instead of in the app. `accept` runs the call once, and the next call is asked again. A decline, a dismissal or five minutes without an answer refuse it with 428 `ACTION_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and `details.reason` `declined`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`: nothing runs, nothing is handed off, and the agent retries only when the person asks. Over Streamable HTTP nobody is asked in the client; a gated call there is handed off and answered `pending_confirmation`, or refused `no_confirmation_service` where the host has no service. The AI service account acts for no person, so its call is refused at every action door with `details.reason: 'service_account'`, and it is neither asked nor handed off: a person runs the action, or its author declares `ai.requiresConfirmation: false` when it is safe unattended. Neither caller sends `confirm`.
